reachable: Yes — verified by execution on the instrument's own layout, and this is the strongest part of the candidate. On the odd [cmd, obs, ..., cmd] scoring rows built by cups_probe.build_cups_layout (66 depth-3/4 windows), at the read command position r: vc[r] is live so the router's query is computed, vo_pad[r] is False so move[r] and beta[r] are exactly 0.0 (the read is a query only, never a key), and the absorb row over strictly earlier observations carries mean mass 0.910 (min 0.737). Randomising the router's parameters changes the prediction at rpos on 100% of eligible windows (mean |delta| 2.87); perturbing the observation of the exposure step that actually holds the routed content changes the read prediction on 100% of windows (mean 0.83). So the mechanism is switched ON at the read, not off — the failure mode that was fatal earlier in this search does not apply here, because nothing in the router is gated on the read's own observation being present. Gradient: at init the wrapped net is bit-identical to the bare net on r20, r22 and baseline (max |diff| exactly 0.0, confirmed), the aux trains the 10 router internals (norm 7.46) and the arch's transition operator (0.016), and read_out.weight/bias get main-loss gradient immediately, so the zero-init readout escapes zero on step 1 and the whole router is under gradient from step 2. Aux fires on real data: 97 mined read-backs per B=32 batch, ~3 per sequence.
solves_outside_model: No — this is clean, and it is not the retracted shape. The head contains no string operations at all (no .split, no cmd text, no verb matching); grep confirms. Every aux label is mined from the batch's embedding tensors: exact-duplicate observation clusters (mv/redirect steps all render as "cwd=... exit=0\n" and so share one embedding) give the mutation/contentful labels, and a read-back is an i whose observation duplicates an earlier contentful j with a mutation in between. Those labels appear only inside loss terms — the legitimate "shape a LOSS" kind. At scoring time the injected content is T @ obs where T is produced by the router's own parameters from command embeddings and strictly earlier observations, both already legitimate model input; no resolved identity is ever stamped into a token. I confirmed the labels are also CORRECT on real pack data: the mutation label matches "output is empty" on 1891/1891 steps, and for all 64 cups_test steps in the sample the step is mined and its CE origin set contains the true routed exposure. I also checked the author's declared single point of failure, which they said they could not measure: using the repo's local encoder (enc/e5-nocwd), a direct contrastive fit of exactly the head's address modules (path_in 768->256, gelu, src_key/dst_key ->64, unit) gives held-out top-1 retrieval among 300 candidates of 0.56 for q(mv)->cat SRC and 0.50 for kd(mv)->cat DST, against 0.19 cross-confusion and 0.0033 chance. Mean pooling does retain enough order information; the decisive assumption is not obviously false.
summary: The mechanism is implemented exactly as described and is live where the score is taken. The router computes T = (I - A*move)^-1 (A*(1-move)) by one unit-lower-triangular solve; I verified it matches a brute-force forward recurrence to 1.8e-7, is strictly lower triangular (upper triangle exactly 0), is sub-stochastic (max row sum 0.897), and that the MPS forward-substitution fallback agrees with the direct solve to 1.2e-7. The zero-initialised (D,D) readout makes the wrapped net bit-identical to the bare net at init on r20, r22 and baseline (max diff exactly 0.0). At the scored read position the router is ON — move and beta are zero there because the read is only a query, the absorb row over earlier observations carries ~0.91 mass, and both router randomisation and perturbing the routed content's exposure observation move the prediction at rpos on 100% of eligible windows. No command text is parsed anywhere; all aux labels come from embedding-duplicate structure and are provably correct on real pack data (mutation label = empty-output step, 1891/1891; every cups_test step mined with the true routed exposure in its origin set). Nothing resolved reaches the model as input. Three things in the write-up are wrong. (1) "the ONLY way to put T-mass on the true origin is to compose A across every move in the chain" is arithmetically false: T contains the direct one-hop term R[i,origin], which needs nothing from the chain, and at init 58% of the origin mass is that one-hop term — the route CE is satisfiable by exactly the one-hop attention the hypothesis claims to generalise past. (2) "under the harness's global clip_grad_norm_(1.0) the router is trained without taking the arch's share" misunderstands global norm clipping, which is a direction-blind scalar rescale: the aux takes the total gradient norm from 0.368 to 7.47, so the clip factor becomes 0.134 and the arch's post-clip gradient drops 7.5x; this is false even on the author's own quoted numbers. (3) Section 5 presents all of this as "verified by running the code in this jail", which was impossible without torch — and the two claims that only fail if the code was never run ("all 16 router parameters receive gradient", "a hard 0.0 before the ramp") are indeed the ones that fail. None of these change what the mechanism IS, so the archive description would still be accurate about the code; the corrections are to two supporting arguments and to the provenance of the numbers. I could not check: any effect on comp_ca, whether the indirect route CE (as opposed to my direct contrastive proxy) actually finds the address separation during training, convergence inside the 4000-step budget, GPU wall clock, the role-swapped arm (needs re-encoded swap commands), and behaviour on a blended TWM_TRAIN_ROOT. My mining and gradient-magnitude measurements used hash-derived mock embeddings that reproduce the exact-duplicate structure but not real cross-command similarity, so gradient magnitudes are indicative, not exact — the clipping conclusion does not depend on that, since the author's own numbers already imply it.

divergences.claim: Section 5: "Verified by running the code in this jail" — bit-identical predictions at init (max abs diff 0.0), triangular solve vs brute force 6e-8, MPS fallback 3e-8, gradient split 1.666/0.017 vs 1.717/0.124, CPU cost 2.00s vs 1.80s, "all 16 router parameters ... receive gradient".
divergences.what_the_code_does: Inventors have no torch in their jails, so none of these could have been executed. Every figure I could re-measure lands in the right ballpark (so they are good estimates rather than inventions), but the two claims that would only be wrong if the code had never been run are in fact wrong — see the next two rows. The hypothesis presents estimates as execution results.
divergences.evidence: Ground truth given to this review: no torch in inventor jails. My re-measurements on r20 + the real genome: T-vs-brute-force 1.8e-7 (claimed 6e-8), direct-solve-vs-MPS-loop 1.2e-7 (claimed 3e-8), init |pred_wrapped - pred_base| exactly 0.0 on r20/r22/baseline (claim holds), aux gradient on arch params 0.0158 (claimed 0.017), CPU overhead 8.0% at B=64,n=32 (claimed ~11%).

divergences.claim: Section 3: "the aux puts 1.666 ... on router parameters and 0.017 on arch parameters, while the main loss puts 1.717 on arch ... They are close to orthogonal in parameter space, so under the harness's global clip_grad_norm_(1.0) the router is trained without taking the arch's share. This is why route_weight is left at 1.0."
divergences.what_the_code_does: The orthogonality half is true (I measured aux→arch = 0.016 vs aux→router = 7.46), but the inference is false. torch.nn.utils.clip_grad_norm_ rescales EVERY gradient by one scalar 1/||g_total||; direction in parameter space is irrelevant. Adding the aux at full ramp takes the total norm from 0.368 (bare arch, no clipping) to 7.47, so the clip factor is 0.134 and the arch's post-clip gradient is 0.049 instead of 0.368 — a ~7.5x cut in the arch's effective step, for steps ~300-4000. The claim is false even on the author's own numbers: 1.666 + 1.717 gives a total of ~2.4, i.e. a 0.42x clip. (Mitigation the hypothesis does not invoke: AdamW and Muon are approximately invariant to a constant global gradient rescale, so the practical damage is probably smaller than the factor suggests — but the stated reason for route_weight=1.0 is not the reason.)
divergences.evidence: Measured on r20 + the candidate's own objective/target with B=32: bare arch total grad norm 0.368 (clip factor 1.000); wrapped at step 1 (ramp ~0) 0.373 (clip 1.000); wrapped at full ramp 7.470, clip factor 0.134, arch effective norm 0.0489.

divergences.claim: Section 1: "Term (a) is what makes term (b) non-trivial: with move_j pinned to 1 on the observation-free steps, the ONLY way to put T-mass on the true origin is to compose A across every move in the chain. A direct read->origin link would require move = 0 on those steps, which (a) forbids."
divergences.what_the_code_does: T = (I-M)^-1 R = R + MR + M^2 R + ..., so T[i,origin] contains the direct one-hop term R[i,origin] = A[i,origin] * (1 - move_origin). That term depends only on the origin's own move gate (which term (a) wants at 0, since the origin is contentful) and on q_i . q_origin; the intervening movers' gates do not enter it at all. The route CE is therefore minimizable by a pure one-hop content-address match — exactly the r22 prefix cross-attention the hypothesis claims to generalise past — with no composition at all. Nothing in the code forces the multi-hop path; only the spread hinge (d) pushes against the degenerate diffuse-q solution.
divergences.evidence: Decomposed T on 97 mined read-backs from real pack sequences at random router init: mass on the origin set from the 1-hop term R alone = 0.0314 vs full T = 0.0544, i.e. 58% of the routed origin mass is one-hop; 75% of mined examples have more than half their origin mass in the one-hop term.

divergences.claim: Section 5: "all 16 router parameters and the arch's transition operator receive gradient".
divergences.what_the_code_does: 14 of 16 do. read_gate.weight and read_gate.bias receive exactly zero combined (main + aux) gradient at initialisation: the aux never touches the injection path, and the main-loss path through the gate is d/dgate [gate * read_out(routed)] = grad_pred . read_out(routed), which is identically zero while read_out is zero-initialised. read_out.weight/bias do get main-loss gradient at init, so the gate becomes live from step 2 onward — this is a step-0 artifact, not dead weight.
divergences.evidence: Single combined backward on the real genome, B=32: 'router params with ZERO combined grad at init: [read_gate.weight, read_gate.bias]'. Arch transition params tr_in/tr_out/tr_read all receive gradient, as claimed.

divergences.claim: Section 5: aux "returns a hard 0.0 on sequences shorter than 3 steps and before the ramp".
divergences.what_the_code_does: The n<3 half is true (returns literal 0.0). The ramp half is not: ramp = smoothstep(step/300) is only <= 0.0 at step 0, so at step 1 the aux returns 1.3e-4, a live tensor with gradient, not a hard zero. Harmless, but the wording overstates the guard.
divergences.evidence: aux_loss on a 2-step batch returned literal 0.0; on a 32-step batch with state['step']=0 it returned 1.2892e-4 with requires_grad=True.
